answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work-linked reputation with stake slashing. Each agent must solve a cipher puzzle tied to its identity before earning trust, and repeat that work, so spawning fake identities costs real compute, not free registration. Honest behavior builds trust slowly, like rock layers forming a mesa, while a bad actor's stake is slashed and its history reset. A public, tamper-evident ledger acts as the onyx seal - durable and hard to forge - so peers verify past work instead of trusting claims. Each extra sybil carries a steep marginal cost, making mass fakery uneconomical.
